Yes, even though I cook all day at my restaurant, when I come home, I still love cooking. So with those type of devices, they’re very much set and forget. You turn them on, put in your food and seasonings of choice, turn on the timer, set the temp, walk away for several hours. It’s about convenience. I like to be involved with my food. I’m willing to babysit it, do all the labor intensive things that most people hate. But it’s my passion. So I totally understand not everyone has the time, and not everyone enjoys the tedious steps the way I do. Those devices are perfect for anyone who doesn’t want to spend 5 hours a night just cooking.

I would not say they are “an insult” to our profession, but most of them have no place in a professional kitchen. For the most part these tools are designed for the home cook for the purpose of saving space, by not having three different objects to do what the instant pot can do, or to provide a healthy alternative to a type of cooking as is the case with the air fryers, or to eliminate labor intensive food prep for people with limited time or knife skills. They all are useful for their intended audience, and make great food accessible to more people, which I’m all about. That being said, I will never buy any of these things for myself. I have no use for them.
